correctness.rationale: The natural three-knot equations leave one interior second derivative. Substitution gives the stated left and right cardinal coefficients. On the left, two coefficients are nonnegative and \(A_2=-t(1-t^2)/(2r(1+r))\le0\), so the data-cube minimum is attained at \((0,0,M)\); maximizing \(t-t^3\) gives \(2/(3\sqrt3)\). The right interval is the reflected calculation with only \(B_0\le0\), giving the \(r^2\) branch. Comparing the two branches yields \(C(r)=\max\{r^{-1},r^2\}/(3\sqrt3(1+r))\), uniquely minimized at \(r=1\) and divergent for skew meshes. Independent rational checks reproduced the basis identities/signs.
residual_risks: The theorem covers exactly three knots and ordinary natural cubic interpolation.
